title: Permission-aware audit exports with faceted query & cursored pagination
creator: Asha Patel
description: Enable console users to run complex, faceted audit queries and export results as CSV/JSON while respecting RBAC v2 policies and SSO/SAML session context. Exports must support cursored pagination for large result sets, preflight permission checks, role-aware redaction, and an optional webhook delivery flow for SIEM ingestion. The feature should be usable from the Audit Viewer search UI and via the saved queries workflow.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A console user can apply multi-facet filters (user, action, resource, time-range, severity, app-token) and see matching results in the Audit Viewer.
AC2: From the viewer, user can start an export (CSV or JSON). A preflight permission check runs and denies exports where the user lacks export permission; denial surface shows policy reason.
AC3: Exports for result sets > 100k rows use cursored pagination (opaque cursor) with consistent sorting; the export endpoint supports NDJSON streaming and chunked CSV generation.
AC4: Exported rows include session context fields when available (sso_session_id, idp), but these fields are redacted according to RBAC policies and tenant-level compliance settings.
AC5: Saved queries in the console persist export preferences and may be re-run; saved queries respect stable query IDs and are revocable by admins.
AC6: Admins can configure an export webhook endpoint; successful export jobs POST a signed, resumable download link and metadata to the webhook for downstream SIEM ingestion.
AC7: Export jobs are accounted in billing/usage dashboard and visible in the Audit Exports console panel with job status, size, and requester.
AC8: All export artifacts follow retention and deletion policies and honor on-prem/private deployment encryption keys (KMS/HSM) when applicable.
implementation_notes: Architecture: implement an 'export gateway' microservice that orchestrates query compilation, permission preflight (OPA policy evaluation against RBAC v2), streaming serialization, and storage/upload to S3 or on-prem artifact store.
Query engine: reuse existing audit search index (time-series elastic/columnar) but add a deterministic sort (timestamp + event_id) to enable stable cursoring across shards.
Cursor design: opaque cursor contains (last_timestamp, last_event_id, tenant_hash, filter_hash, server_version); sign cursor with HMAC to prevent tampering.

Redaction: integrate with redaction rules service. Preflight returns redaction map per column; export gateway applies redaction server-side during serialization to avoid leaking suppressed fields in multipart downloads.

Permission semantics: RBAC v2 policy must define 'audit:export' with optional attribute-level allow/deny. For SSO sessions, map idp groups to RBAC roles in evaluation context so session-scoped permissions are applied.
SSO/SAML nuance: preserve minimal session metadata in export artifacts based on compliance flag; never include raw SAML assertions. For on-prem, respect customer KMS for signing download URLs.
Webhook: deliver a small job-complete payload (signed URL, job_id, row_count, filter_digest). Retries with exponential backoff; include HMAC signature header for authenticity.
Rate-limits & quotas: enforce per-tenant concurrent export job caps and enqueue large jobs to background worker pool to avoid overloading query tier.

Observability: add tracing spans (query-compile, preflight, serialization), metrics (rows_exported, bytes_exported, job_duration), and an audit event for export job creation/completion with requester id.
Backward compatibility: existing 'download current view' flows should be routed to the export gateway but maintain same immediate-response UX for small result sets (<10k rows).
testing_plan: Unit tests: policy evaluation stubs for RBAC v2, cursor serialization/deserialization, redaction pipeline tests for CSV and JSON.
Integration tests: run exports against a seeded audit index with mixed tenants and verify role-aware redaction, cursor correctness (no duplicates/misses), and webhook delivery flow.
E2E: simulate SSO user (SAML) with groups -> role mapping and confirm session metadata handling and policy enforcement in exports.
Load test: create 500 concurrent small export jobs and 10 long-running large export jobs to validate worker pool behavior and export queueing.
Security tests: penetration tests on signed cursors, HMAC header verification for webhook, and KMS integration checks for on-prem signing.
Manual QA: UX review for preflight permission denial messages and admin panel flows for revoking saved queries and webhook configuration.
Compliance: validate retention/deletion flows trigger KMS key-access checks and that exported artifacts are removed when tenant retention expires.
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (canary): Enable gateway for 10% of orgs and log policy evaluation traces. Provide feature flag to disable webhook delivery per-tenant.
Phase 2: Open to all orgs, expose saved query export preferences in console, and surface export job history in Audit Exports panel.
Phase 3: Enable webhook by default and add export quota alerts in cost dashboards.
Rollback: revert feature flag to route exports to legacy path (small-exports only) and cancel queued jobs in gateway; ensure consumers are notified via webhook cancellation events.
